cases.report_quote: the middleware is mounted before all three routes, so every route is gated before dispatch.
cases.reason: Correctly says the bearer middleware precedes every /mcp handler. It makes no unauthenticated-access claim and invents no OAuth audience gap.

cases.report_quote: Nothing was executed or tested. This is a source read only and is not deployment authorization.
cases.reason: Makes no runtime, crash or deployed-secret claims. Gateway, TLS, audit and supervision are listed as not reviewed and needing host evidence.

cases.report_quote: Both GET and DELETE use the `route` wrapper at line 15, so rejections reach `next`.
cases.reason: Recognizes the async rejection forwarding and alleges no uncaught-rejection defect. It treats session IDs as randomUUID values and alleges no inherited-key defect.

cases.report_quote: | `GET /mcp` | Auth, session lookup, rejection handling | Assessed |
cases.reason: Assesses auth, session lookup by header and rejection handling for GET, with line references and the 404 path.
Assesses DELETE separately. It notes the same lookup as GET, the shared route wrapper, and that no map entry is removed.

cases.report_quote: `launch.json` only names the entrypoint, the export and the factory.
cases.reason: Resolves the launch entrypoint, export and factory. It separates the in-scope module from the external createTransport and handleRequest, which it marks not reviewed.
Assesses POST init: session creation via randomUUID, storage of the external transport, the auth gate, and unbounded growth.

additional_supported_gaps: F1: sessions are never deleted or bounded, and the DELETE handler leaves the map entry in place (routes.mjs:12, 21-25).
F2: the bearer comparison uses !== instead of a constant-time comparison (routes.mjs:7).
No lockfile, so transitive dependencies are not reproducible.
notes: The report flags supplier-notes.txt:1 as an untrusted injection and ignores it. Its line references match routes.mjs. External claims (Express, Node, mcpb manifest, GHSA, MCP security guidance) cite research/ sources with dates. The SDK advisory is correctly ruled not applicable because package.json has no MCP dependency. F1 to F3 are low or conditional and stated as such. The one minor weakness is that the Origin/Host item (F3) is informational and rests on general MCP guidance. The report states that nothing was tested and gives no deployment authorization.
